name: Stonewrought Dam
summary: Along Loch Modan’s northern rim, waters gather behind Stonewrought Dam. The dwarven barrier holds back the Loch and drains the Wetlands below into habitable marshes.

sections.title: A Wonder of Dwarven Craft
sections.body: East of Dun Algaz, Stonewrought Dam spans a canyon in one of the great works of dwarven craft. Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright designed it and pioneered the stonewrought technique used to raise it. By holding water in the mountain basin, the dam doubled the Loch’s surface area and steadily lowered the waters to the north. The Wetlands formed from a valley once wholly flooded.

sections.title: Sabotage and Defense
sections.body: Stonewrought Dam now serves Ironforge, but Dark Iron saboteurs from the southern mountains target it. After recent assaults and attempts to slip inside, Ironforge placed a garrison here under Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Guards and engineers patrol the masonry day and night. Should the dam be breached, the Loch could drain and send a devastating flood across the Wetlands below.

faq.answer: Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright designed and oversaw Stonewrought Dam. He pioneered the stonewrought technique used to build it. Though a Dark Iron master built it, the dam serves the Bronzebeard kingdom today.

faq.q: What happens if the dam breaks?
faq.answer: If Stonewrought Dam collapsed, the Loch would rapidly drain and leave Loch Modan an empty crater of mud. Its waters would then sweep into the Wetlands in a devastating, uncontrollable flood.

faq.q: Why are Dark Iron dwarves attacking it?
faq.answer: The Dark Iron clan attacks Ironforge’s vital works to destabilize the region. Crippling the dam would cripple supply lines, drown the northern Wetlands and strike a bitter blow against Bronzebeard pride.

faq.q: Who is currently in charge of the dam's defense?
faq.answer: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII manages the dam’s daily operations and defenses. He coordinates with Ironforge forces to root out saboteurs.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you can see the dam as a monument to dwarven masonry and ingenuity. Its Dark Iron heritage remains a sore point contested among Ironforge’s historians.
As an engineer, you can study the dam’s hydraulic controls and stonewrought load-bearing mechanics. Its design rivals the great works beneath Ironforge.
